content:
maya: Heads-up — after promoting the qlora 4-bit build of siren-6b to 10% canary we started seeing token-merge artifacts and occasional short-loop repetition. Example outputs from user-facing prompt below. :eyes:

maya: Generated (weird):
```
Q: How do I reset my password?
A: To reset your password, go to the settings page and click thepasswordreset link. Then followthe instructions to verify youremail and setanewpassword.
```

maya: Notice tokens like `thepasswordreset`, `followthe`, `setanewpassword` — merged without spaces, and also some mid-sentence collapse. Not all generations show it but enough to fail a few eval prompts.

raj: Could be tokenizer mismatch or failing tokenizer merges post-quant. Which tokenizer commit did we ship? Any custom merges?

maya: Shipping with tokenizer v2.1.4 (same as baseline). No custom merges in our onboarding config. Model commit: sha ab12c3f (qlora weights + quant config).

zach: ops-bot: deploy canary siren-6b qlora-4bit @ 2026-03-18T14:23Z to 10% (ids: canary-319).

li: Two quick hypotheses: 1) quantized token embeddings / embedding table aliasing causing adjacent token collapse; 2) batching/kv cache mixing where session boundaries overlap under continuous batching. We saw similar in ember7b coldstart issue (but not identical).

li: Quick repro steps I ran locally:
```bash
# simple curl to hosted canary
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $CANARY_KEY" \
  -d '{"model":"siren-6b-qlora-canary","input":"How do I reset my password?","max_tokens":80,"temp":0.2}'
```

li: I reproduced the merged-token behavior with concurrent requests (3x parallel). When I forced sequential single requests it was much rarer.

raj: Good catch. If concurrent request batching is sewing together KV caches it's a runtime routing bug. Can we quickly test disabling batching for the canary model?

maya: I can patch the model config now to set max_batch_size=1 and disable prefix caching. Will do in ~5m and post results.

zach: ops-bot: Applied config patch to siren-6b-qlora-canary: {"max_batch_size":1,"kv_cache_enabled":false}. Rolling apply.

eva: Also try generating with fp16 checkpoint to confirm whether quantization is amplifying the symptom. If fp16 is clean, that points at quantization/embedding lookup issues.

raj: I'll spin a job to run a small eval harness across the canary prompt set: 500 prompts, compare tokenization boundaries, and diff against baseline fp16. I will post a summary in ~30m.

maya: After disabling batching I ran the exact failing prompt 50x in parallel and now I only see 1/50 with merge. Seems dramatically reduced. Keeping canary at 10% but disabling batching for now.

maya: For next steps: (1) raj will run quantitative eval vs fp16, (2) li to check runtime routing / batch key derivation for any hash collision, (3) eva to try repro on local quant kernels with deterministic seed, (4) if confirmed, revert to fp16 for the broader rollout.

raj: On it. I'll share the CSV of token-boundary diffs when done. ETA 25–40m.

li: If we find batch key bug, short-term mitigation could be to force per-request session ids or keep max_batch_size=1 for canary until fixed. Also consider re-exporting quantized embeddings with different alignment.

maya: Thanks — flagging this for postmortem if it ends up kernel/routing related. Will update the canary ticket and the onboarding checklist to include a concurrent-batching token-boundary smoke test going forward. :thumbsup:
